import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable forking conjecture for simple theories

The formulation below is the stable-forking conjecture used by Kim--Pillay and Peretz:
every instance of forking in a complete simple first-order theory is witnessed by a stable
formula over the base set. The definitions are semantic, in the ambient model conventionally
taken to be a monster model. Finite tuples are represented by `Fin n`.

A possibly imaginary element is covered by applying the statement to the usual one-sorted
coding of $T^{\mathrm{eq}}$, in which it is an element of a home sort. This fixes the
$L(A)$, rather than parameter-free $L$, version of the conjecture.

*References:*
- [Assaf Peretz, *Geometry of forking in simple theories*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412356)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {M : Type w} [L.Structure M]

/-- The valuation of a formula whose variables consist of indexed base parameters, an
`x`-tuple, and a `y`-tuple. -/
def parameterValuation {ι : Type*} (base : ι → M) {m n : ℕ}
    (a : Fin m → M) (b : Fin n → M) : ι ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin n → M
  | Sum.inl c => base c
  | Sum.inr (Sum.inl i) => a i
  | Sum.inr (Sum.inr j) => b j

/-- A sequence of `n`-tuples is indiscernible over the image of `base` if increasing finite
subsequences have the same type over those parameters. -/
def IndiscernibleOver {ι : Type*} (base : ι → M) {n : ℕ}
    (b : ℕ → Fin n → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (ι ⊕ (Fin k × Fin n)))
    (i j : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono i → StrictMono j →
      φ.Realize (fun z => match z with
        | Sum.inl c => base c
        | Sum.inr r => b (i r.1) r.2) ↔
      φ.Realize (fun z => match z with
        | Sum.inl c => base c
        | Sum.inr r => b (j r.1) r.2)

/-- A formula instance divides over the image of `base` if its parameter tuple starts an
indiscernible sequence whose corresponding instances have a finite inconsistent subfamily. -/
def DividesOver (base : ι → M) {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (ι ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin n))
    (b : Fin n → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (bseq : ℕ → Fin n → M) (k : ℕ),
    bseq 0 = b ∧ IndiscernibleOver (L := L) base bseq ∧ 0 < k ∧
    ∀ (i : Fin k → ℕ), Function.Injective i →
      ¬ ∃ a : Fin m → M, ∀ r : Fin k,
        φ.Realize (parameterValuation base a (bseq (i r)))

/-- A formula instance forks over `A` if, in an elementary extension, it implies a finite
disjunction of formula instances that divide over the embedded copy of `A`. -/
def ForksOver (A : Set M) {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (A ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin n))
    (b : Fin n → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v w} (L.completeTheory M))
    (e : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (p r : ℕ)
    (θ : Fin r → L.Formula (A ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin p)) (c : Fin r → Fin p → N),
      (∀ i, DividesOver (L := L) (fun z : A => e z) (θ i) (c i)) ∧
      ∀ a : Fin m → N,
        φ.Realize (parameterValuation (fun z : A => e z) a (e ∘ b)) →
          ∃ i, (θ i).Realize (parameterValuation (fun z : A => e z) a (c i))

/-- A formula over `A` is stable if it has no infinite order pattern
`ψ(aᵢ,bⱼ) ↔ i ≤ j` in any elementary extension containing the parameters. -/
def StableOver (A : Set M) {m n : ℕ} (ψ : L.Formula (A ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v w} (L.completeTheory M))
    (e : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (a : ℕ → Fin m → N) (b : ℕ → Fin n → N),
      ∀ i j, ψ.Realize (parameterValuation (fun z : A => e z) (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- A formula has the tree property in `M` if its parameters can be placed on the tree
`ℕ^{<ω}` so that every branch is finitely consistent and the immediate successors of every
node are uniformly finitely inconsistent. -/
def HasTreePropertyIn (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] {m n : ℕ}
    (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (b : List ℕ → Fin n → M) (k : ℕ), 0 < k ∧
    (∀ branch : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ q : ℕ,
      ∃ a : Fin m → M, ∀ t < q,
        φ.Realize (Sum.elim a (b (List.ofFn fun i : Fin t => branch i)))) ∧
    ∀ node : List ℕ, ∀ children : Fin k → ℕ, Function.Injective children →
      ¬ ∃ a : Fin m → M, ∀ i : Fin k,
        φ.Realize (Sum.elim a (b (node ++ [children i])))

/-- A theory has the tree property if some formula has the tree property in a model of the
theory. -/
def HasTreeProperty (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (m n : ℕ)
    (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)),
    HasTreePropertyIn M φ

/-- A first-order theory is simple if no formula has the tree property. -/
def IsSimple (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ¬ HasTreeProperty T

/--
**Stable forking conjecture for simple theories (Kim--Pillay/Peretz formulation).**

Every complete simple first-order theory has stable forking. More precisely, in an ambient
monster model of such a theory, for every parameter set $A$ and tuples $a,b$, if
$a \not\mathrel{\perp}_A b$ (that is, some formula in $\operatorname{tp}(a/Ab)$ forks over
$A$), then there is a stable formula $\psi(x,y) \in L(A)$ such that $\psi(a,b)$ holds and
$\psi(x,b)$ forks over $A$. Here stable means that there are no infinite sequences
$(a_i),(b_j)$ with $\psi(a_i,b_j)$ if and only if $i \le j$. Applying the assertion to
$T^{\mathrm{eq}}$ includes possibly imaginary $a$ and $b$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem stable_forking_conjecture_for_simple_theories
    (T : L.Theory) (hcomplete : T.IsComplete) (hsimple : IsSimple T)
    (M : Type w) [Nonempty M] [L.Structure M] [M ⊨ T] :
    ∀ (A : Set M) (m n : ℕ) (a : Fin m → M) (b : Fin n → M),
      (∃ φ : L.Formula (A ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin n),
        φ.Realize (parameterValuation (fun z : A => (z : M)) a b) ∧ ForksOver A φ b) →
      ∃ ψ : L.Formula (A ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin n),
        StableOver A ψ ∧
          ψ.Realize (parameterValuation (fun z : A => (z : M)) a b) ∧ ForksOver A ψ b := by
  sorry

end StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The stable forking conjecture for simple theories

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory. A formula $\varphi(x, y)$ has the *tree property* if
there are $k < \omega$ and parameters $(b_\eta : \eta \in \omega^{<\omega})$ such that for every
node $\eta$ the set $\{\varphi(x, b_{\eta \frown i}) : i < \omega\}$ is $k$-inconsistent, while
for every branch $\sigma \in \omega^\omega$ the set $\{\varphi(x, b_{\sigma | n}) : n < \omega\}$
is consistent. $T$ is *simple* if no formula has the tree property.

A formula $\varphi(x, b)$ *divides* over a set $A$ if there are $k < \omega$ and a sequence
$(b_i : i < \omega)$ of realizations of $\operatorname{tp}(b / A)$ such that
$\{\varphi(x, b_i) : i < \omega\}$ is $k$-inconsistent. It *forks* over $A$ if it implies a finite
disjunction of formulas each of which divides over $A$. We write $a \not\downarrow_A b$ if some
formula of $\operatorname{tp}(a / A b)$ forks over $A$. A formula $\psi(x, y)$ is *stable* if there
are no sequences $(a_i : i < \omega)$, $(b_j : j < \omega)$ with $\psi(a_i, b_j)$ iff $i \le j$.

Following Kim–Pillay and Peretz, $T$ has *stable forking* if whenever $a \not\downarrow_A b$ there
is a stable formula $\psi(x, y) \in L(A)$ with $\psi(a, b)$ such that $\psi(x, b)$ forks over $A$.
The stable forking conjecture asserts that every simple theory has stable forking.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [A. Peretz, *Geometry of forking in simple theories*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412356),
  Definition (items 3 and 4) and the sentence following it.
- B. Kim and A. Pillay, *Around stable forking*, Fundamenta Mathematicae 170 (2001), 107–118.
-/

universe u v w

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {M : Type w} [L.Structure M] {α β : Type*}

/-- `Divides θ b` says that the formula `θ(x, b)` divides (over `∅`): there are `k < ω` and, in
some elementary extension `N` of `M`, a sequence `(c i : i < ω)` of realizations of the type of
`b` over `∅` such that `{θ(x, c i) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent, i.e. no `k` of these formulas
have a common realization.

Dividing over a set of parameters `A ⊆ M` is obtained by applying this to the language `L[[A]]`. -/
def Divides (θ : L.Formula (α ⊕ β)) (b : β → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (c : ℕ → β → N) (k : ℕ),
    (∀ (i : ℕ) (χ : L.Formula β), χ.Realize (c i) ↔ χ.Realize (f ∘ b)) ∧
    ∀ s : Finset ℕ, s.card = k → ¬ ∃ x : α → N, ∀ i ∈ s, θ.Realize (Sum.elim x (c i))

/-- `Forks θ b` says that the formula `θ(x, b)` forks (over `∅`): in some elementary extension `N`
of `M` there are finitely many formulas `χ j (x, c j)`, with parameters `c j` from `N`, each of
which divides over `∅`, such that `θ(x, b)` implies their disjunction.

Forking over a set of parameters `A ⊆ M` is obtained by applying this to the language `L[[A]]`. -/
def Forks (θ : L.Formula (α ⊕ β)) (b : β → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (n : ℕ)
    (χ : Fin n → Σ m : ℕ, L.Formula (α ⊕ Fin m)) (c : ∀ j, Fin (χ j).1 → N),
    (∀ j, Divides (χ j).2 (c j)) ∧
    ∀ x : α → N, θ.Realize (Sum.elim x (f ∘ b)) → ∃ j, (χ j).2.Realize (Sum.elim x (c j))

variable (L) in
/-- `Indep L A a b` says that `a` is independent from `b` over `A`, written `a ⫝_A b`: no formula
of the type of `a` over `A ∪ b`, i.e. no formula `χ(x, b)` with `χ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` and `χ(a, b)`,
forks over `A`. -/
def Indep (A : Set M) (a : α → M) (b : β → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ χ : L[[A]].Formula (α ⊕ β), χ.Realize (Sum.elim a b) → ¬ Forks χ b

/-- `IsStable M ψ` says that the formula `ψ(x, y)` is stable in the theory of `M`: in no elementary
extension `N` of `M` are there sequences `(a i : i < ω)`, `(b j : j < ω)` such that
`ψ(a i, b j)` holds iff `i ≤ j`.

Stability of a formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` with parameters from `A ⊆ M` is obtained by applying this
to the language `L[[A]]`. -/
def IsStable (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] (ψ : L.Formula (α ⊕ β)) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (_ : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (a : ℕ → α → N) (b : ℕ → β → N),
    ∀ i j, ψ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- `HasTreeProperty T φ` says that the formula `φ(x, y)` has the tree property in `T`: in some
model `N` of `T` there are `k < ω` and parameters `(b η : η ∈ ω^{<ω})` such that for every node `η`
the set `{φ(x, b (η ⌢ i)) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent, and for every branch `σ ∈ ω^ω` the set
`{φ(x, b (σ | n)) : n < ω}` is consistent (i.e. finitely satisfiable in `N`). -/
def HasTreeProperty (T : L.Theory) (φ : L.Formula (α ⊕ β)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (b : List ℕ → β → N) (k : ℕ),
    (∀ (η : List ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ), s.card = k →
      ¬ ∃ x : α → N, ∀ i ∈ s, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (b (η ++ [i])))) ∧
    ∀ (σ : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ), ∃ x : α → N, ∀ m < n, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (b ((List.range m).map σ)))

/-- A theory `T` is simple if no formula `φ(x, y)` has the tree property in `T`. -/
def IsSimple (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n m : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)), ¬ HasTreeProperty T φ

/-- A formula that divides forks. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem forks_of_divides {m : ℕ} (θ : L.Formula (α ⊕ Fin m)) (b : Fin m → M) (h : Divides θ b) :
    Forks θ b := by
  obtain ⟨N, _, f, c, k, hc, hk⟩ := h
  refine ⟨N, inferInstance, f, 1, fun _ => ⟨m, θ⟩, fun _ => f ∘ b, fun _ => ?_, fun x hx => ⟨0, hx⟩⟩
  exact ⟨N, inferInstance, ElementaryEmbedding.refl L N, c, k, fun i χ => by simpa using hc i χ, hk⟩

/-- **The stable forking conjecture for simple theories** (Kim–Pillay; Peretz).

Every complete simple theory `T` has stable forking: for every model `M` of `T`, every set of
parameters `A ⊆ M` and all (finite tuples) `a`, `b` in `M` with `a ⫝̸_A b`, there is a stable
formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` such that `ψ(a, b)` holds and `ψ(x, b)` forks over `A`.

Here `a ⫝̸_A b` means that some formula of `tp(a / A ∪ b)` forks over `A`. Independence, forking and
stability are invariant under elementary extensions, so ranging over all models `M` of `T` is the
same as working in a monster model. Peretz allows `a`, `b` to be imaginary; since the conjecture
ranges over all simple theories and `T^eq` is simple whenever `T` is, the version for real tuples
stated here is equivalent to the version with imaginaries. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem stable_forking_conjecture_for_simple_theories {T : L.Theory}
    (hT : T.IsComplete) (hsimple : IsSimple T) (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) (A : Set M)
    {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M) (hab : ¬ Indep L A a b) :
    ∃ ψ : L[[A]].Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m),
      IsStable M ψ ∧ ψ.Realize (Sum.elim a b) ∧ Forks ψ b := by
  sorry

end StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The stable forking conjecture for simple theories

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory. A formula $\psi(x, y)$ (possibly with parameters) is
*stable* if there are no sequences $(a_i)_{i < \omega}$, $(b_j)_{j < \omega}$ (in a model of $T$)
with $\psi(a_i, b_j)$ if and only if $i \le j$. The theory $T$ is *simple* if no formula
$\varphi(x, y)$ has the tree property.

An instance of forking $a \not\perp_A b$ (i.e. $\operatorname{tp}(a / Ab)$ forks over $A$) is
*stable* if it is witnessed by a stable formula: there is a stable formula $\psi(x, y) \in L(A)$
such that $\psi(a, b)$ holds and $\psi(x, b)$ forks over $A$. The theory $T$ *satisfies stable
forking* if every instance of forking is stable.

The **stable forking conjecture** (Kim–Pillay) states that every simple theory satisfies stable
forking. We formalize the version given in Peretz's paper (Definition, item 4 and the sentence
following it): the witnessing formula may have parameters from the base set $A$.

Forking, dividing, indiscernibility and stability are usually defined inside a monster model.
Here they are defined inside an arbitrary model `M` of `T`, with the relevant sequences and
parameters taken in an elementary extension of `M`; by compactness this is equivalent.
Since every complete simple theory `T` is quantified over, and the conjecture applies in
particular to (a single-sorted coding of) `T^{eq}`, the restriction to real tuples is harmless.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
- A. Peretz, *Geometry of forking in simple theories*, [arXiv:math/0412356](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412356)
- B. Kim, A. Pillay, *Around stable forking*, Fund. Math. 170 (2001), 107–118
-/

namespace StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {M : Type w} [L.Structure M]

/-- The formula `ψ(x, y, c)`, with parameters `c` from `M`, is *stable* if there are no
sequences `(aᵢ)`, `(bⱼ)` in an elementary extension `N` of `M` such that `ψ(aᵢ, bⱼ, c)` holds
if and only if `i ≤ j`. -/
def IsStableFormula {n m k : ℕ} (ψ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N)
    (a : ℕ → Fin n → N) (b : ℕ → Fin m → N),
    ∀ i j, ψ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (Sum.elim (b j) (f ∘ c))) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- The formula `x = y` is stable. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isStableFormula_equal :
    IsStableFormula ((Term.var (Sum.inl 0)).equal (Term.var (Sum.inr (Sum.inl 0))) :
      L.Formula (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 0)) (M := M) finZeroElim := by
  rintro ⟨N, _, f, a, b, h⟩
  simp only [Formula.realize_equal, Term.realize_var, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr] at h
  have h00 := (h 0 0).2 le_rfl
  have h01 := (h 0 1).2 zero_le_one
  have h11 := (h 1 1).2 le_rfl
  exact absurd ((h 1 0).1 (h11.trans (h01.symm.trans h00))) (by norm_num)

/-- The formula `φ(x, y)` has the *tree property* with respect to the theory `T` if there are
`k` and a tree `(b_η)_{η ∈ ω^{<ω}}` of parameter tuples in some model of `T` such that
for every node `η` the family `{φ(x, b_{η⌢i}) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent, and for every
branch `σ ∈ ω^ω` the set `{φ(x, b_{σ|j}) : j < ω}` is consistent (finitely satisfiable). -/
def HasTreeProperty (T : L.Theory) {n m : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (k : ℕ) (b : List ℕ → Fin m → N),
    (∀ (η : List ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ), s.card = k →
      ¬ ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ i ∈ s, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (b (η ++ [i])))) ∧
    ∀ (σ : ℕ → ℕ) (l : ℕ), ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ j < l, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (b ((List.range j).map σ)))

/-- A theory `T` is *simple* if no formula `φ(x, y)` has the tree property. -/
def IsSimple (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n m : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)), ¬ HasTreeProperty T φ

/-- The tree property is witnessed in a model, so a theory without models is (vacuously) simple. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isSimple_of_not_isSatisfiable {T : L.Theory} (hT : ¬ T.IsSatisfiable) : IsSimple T := by
  rintro n m φ ⟨N, -⟩
  exact hT ⟨N⟩

variable (L) in
/-- A sequence `(dᵢ)_{i < ω}` of tuples in `M` is *indiscernible over* a set `B ⊆ M` if for
every formula `θ(y₀, …, y_{l-1}, z)` and every tuple `c` of parameters from `B`, the truth value
of `θ(d_{i₀}, …, d_{i_{l-1}}, c)` is the same for all increasing index tuples `i₀ < ⋯ < i_{l-1}`.
-/
def IsIndiscernibleOver {β : Type*} (B : Set M) (d : ℕ → β → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (l k : ℕ) (θ : L.Formula (Fin l × β ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M), (∀ i, c i ∈ B) →
    ∀ (i j : Fin l → ℕ), StrictMono i → StrictMono j →
      (θ.Realize (Sum.elim (fun p => d (i p.1) p.2) c) ↔
        θ.Realize (Sum.elim (fun p => d (j p.1) p.2) c))

/-- The formula `φ(x, d)`, with parameters `d` from `M`, *divides over* a set `A ⊆ M` if in some
elementary extension `N` of `M` there is a sequence `(dᵢ)_{i < ω}` indiscernible over `A` with
`d₀ = d` such that `{φ(x, dᵢ) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent for some `k`. -/
def Divides {n : ℕ} {β : Type*} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (d : β → M) (A : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (d' : ℕ → β → N) (k : ℕ),
    d' 0 = f ∘ d ∧ IsIndiscernibleOver L (f '' A) d' ∧
    ∀ s : Finset ℕ, s.card = k → ¬ ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ i ∈ s, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (d' i))

/-- The formula `φ(x, d)`, with parameters `d` from `M`, *forks over* a set `A ⊆ M` if it implies
a finite disjunction `⋁ᵢ ψᵢ(x, eᵢ)` of formulas, each of which divides over `A`. The parameters
`eᵢ` may lie in an elementary extension `N` of `M`. -/
def Forks {n : ℕ} {β : Type*} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (d : β → M) (A : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (l : ℕ) (m : Fin l → ℕ)
    (ψ : ∀ i, L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin (m i))) (e : ∀ i, Fin (m i) → N),
    (∀ i, Divides (ψ i) (e i) (f '' A)) ∧
    ∀ x : Fin n → N, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (f ∘ d)) → ∃ i, (ψ i).Realize (Sum.elim x (e i))

variable (L) in
/-- The tuple `a` is *independent from* the tuple `b` *over* the set `A ⊆ M`, written
`a ⫝_A b`, if the type `tp(a / A b)` does not fork over `A`: no formula `φ(x, b, c)` with
`c` from `A` that is satisfied by `a` forks over `A`. -/
def IsIndependent {n m : ℕ} (A : Set M) (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M),
    (∀ i, c i ∈ A) ∧ φ.Realize (Sum.elim a (Sum.elim b c)) ∧ Forks φ (Sum.elim b c) A

/-- **The stable forking conjecture for simple theories** (Kim–Pillay; in the form of Peretz,
arXiv:math/0412356, Definition item 4): every complete simple theory `T` satisfies stable forking.
That is, for every model `M` of `T`, every set `A ⊆ M` and all tuples `a`, `b` in `M` with
`a ⫝̸_A b`, there is a stable formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` (i.e. `ψ(x, y, c)` with `c` from `A`)
such that `ψ(a, b)` holds and `ψ(x, b)` forks over `A`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem stable_forking_conjecture_for_simple_theories {T : L.Theory} (hT : T.IsComplete)
    (hsimple : IsSimple T) [M ⊨ T] (A : Set M) {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M)
    (hab : ¬ IsIndependent L A a b) :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (ψ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M),
      (∀ i, c i ∈ A) ∧ IsStableFormula ψ c ∧ ψ.Realize (Sum.elim a (Sum.elim b c)) ∧
      Forks ψ (Sum.elim b c) A := by
  sorry

end StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The stable forking conjecture for simple theories

The stable forking conjecture asserts that in a simple theory every instance of forking is
witnessed by a stable formula. The precise version stated here is the one of Kim and Pillay
(2001), as recorded in Peretz (Definition, item 4):

A complete theory `T` *satisfies stable forking* if for all (tuples) `a`, `b` and all parameter
sets `A` in a model of `T` with `a ⫝̸_A b` (i.e. `tp(a/Ab)` forks over `A`), there is a
*stable* formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` such that `ψ(a, b)` holds and `ψ(x, b)` forks over `A`.
Here `ψ(x, y)` is *stable* if there are no sequences `(a_i)_{i < ω}`, `(b_j)_{j < ω}` with
`ψ(a_i, b_j) ↔ i ≤ j`, and `T` is *simple* if no formula has the tree property.

The conjecture: every complete simple theory satisfies stable forking.

Several inequivalent formulations appear in the literature (formulas in `L` versus `L(A)`,
types over `B ⊇ A`, `T^eq` and hyperimaginaries, "weak" stable forking), and counterexamples are
known to some of them. This file fixes the Kim–Pillay/Peretz formulation above.

Peretz works in `T^eq` (with imaginary elements). Since `T^eq` is itself a complete simple
theory (after the standard one-sorted encoding), the statement "every complete simple theory
satisfies stable forking" is the same whether or not imaginaries are allowed, so the
formalisation below only uses tuples of real elements.

All definitions are given semantically, relative to a model `M` and its elementary extensions
(playing the role of the monster model); by compactness this agrees with the usual definitions
in a monster model. As for `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`, elementary extensions of
`M : Type w` are taken in `Type (max u v w)`, where `L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
- A. Peretz, *Geometry of forking in simple theories*, [arXiv:math/0412356](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412356)
- B. Kim and A. Pillay, *Around stable forking*, Fund. Math. 170 (2001), 107–118.
-/

universe u v w

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {M : Type w} [L.Structure M] {N : Type*} [L.Structure N]

/-- `RealizesTypeOver f A e e'` says that the tuple `e'` (in an elementary extension `N` of `M`
along `f`) realizes the type `tp(e/A)` of the tuple `e` over the set `A ⊆ M`: every `L`-formula
with parameters from `A` satisfied by `e` in `M` is satisfied by `e'` in `N`, and conversely. -/
def RealizesTypeOver {β : Type*} (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (A : Set M) (e : β → M) (e' : β → N) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (θ : L.Formula (β ⊕ Fin k)) (d : Fin k → M), (∀ i, d i ∈ A) →
    (θ.Realize (Sum.elim e' (f ∘ d)) ↔ θ.Realize (Sum.elim e d))

/-- `Divides A φ e` says that the formula `φ(x, e)` (with `x` a tuple of `n` variables and
parameters `e` from `M`) *divides over* `A ⊆ M`: in some elementary extension `N` of `M` there
is a sequence `(e_i)_{i < ω}` of realizations of `tp(e/A)` and a `k` such that
`{φ(x, e_i) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent, i.e. no `k` of these formulas have a common
realization. -/
def Divides {n : ℕ} {β : Type*} (A : Set M) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (e : β → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (e' : ℕ → β → N),
    (∀ i, RealizesTypeOver f A e (e' i)) ∧
      ∀ s : Finset ℕ, s.card = k → ¬ ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ i ∈ s, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (e' i))

/-- `Forks A φ e` says that the formula `φ(x, e)` (with parameters `e` from `M`) *forks over*
`A ⊆ M`: in some elementary extension `N` of `M` there are finitely many formulas
`ψ_1(x, d_1), …, ψ_r(x, d_r)` with parameters `d_i` from `N`, each dividing over `A`, such that
`φ(x, e)` implies `ψ_1(x, d_1) ∨ … ∨ ψ_r(x, d_r)`. -/
def Forks {n : ℕ} {β : Type*} (A : Set M) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (e : β → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (r : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ)
    (ψ : (i : Fin r) → L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin (m i))) (d : (i : Fin r) → Fin (m i) → N),
    (∀ i, Divides (f '' A) (ψ i) (d i)) ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n → N, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (f ∘ e)) → ∃ i, (ψ i).Realize (Sum.elim x (d i))

variable (L) in
/-- `TypeForksOver L A a b` says that `tp(a/A ∪ b)` *forks over* `A`, written `a ⫝̸_A b`
(`a` is not independent from `b` over `A`): some `L`-formula `φ(x, b, c)` with parameters
`c` from `A` is satisfied by `a` and forks over `A`. -/
def TypeForksOver {n m : ℕ} (A : Set M) (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M),
    (∀ i, c i ∈ A) ∧ φ.Realize (Sum.elim a (Sum.elim b c)) ∧ Forks A φ (Sum.elim b c)

/-- `IsStableFormula ψ c` says that the formula `ψ(x, y, c)` with parameters `c` from `M`
(an `L(A)`-formula when the `c i` lie in `A`) is *stable*: there are no sequences
`(a_i)_{i < ω}`, `(b_j)_{j < ω}` (in any elementary extension of `M`) such that
`ψ(a_i, b_j, c)` holds if and only if `i ≤ j`. -/
def IsStableFormula {n m k : ℕ} (ψ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (a : ℕ → Fin n → N)
    (b : ℕ → Fin m → N), ∀ i j, ψ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (Sum.elim (b j) (f ∘ c))) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- `HasTreeProperty T φ` says that the formula `φ(x, y)` has the *tree property* with respect
to the theory `T`: there are `k < ω`, a model `N` of `T` and a tree `(a_η)_{η ∈ ω^{<ω}}` of
tuples of `N` such that
* for every branch `η ∈ ω^ω`, the set `{φ(x, a_{η|l}) : l < ω}` is consistent (realized in `N`);
* for every node `η ∈ ω^{<ω}`, the set `{φ(x, a_{η⌢i}) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent.

Finite sequences `η ∈ ω^{<ω}` are encoded as lists, `η|l` is `List.ofFn fun i : Fin l ↦ η i`
and `η⌢i` is `η ++ [i]`. -/
def HasTreeProperty {n m : ℕ} (T : L.Theory) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (N : Type (max u v)) (_ : L.Structure N) (_ : N ⊨ T) (a : List ℕ → Fin m → N),
    (∀ η : ℕ → ℕ, ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ l : ℕ,
      φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (a (List.ofFn fun i : Fin l ↦ η i)))) ∧
    ∀ (η : List ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ), s.card = k →
      ¬ ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ i ∈ s, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (a (η ++ [i])))

/-- A theory `T` is *simple* if no formula `φ(x, y)` has the tree property with respect to `T`. -/
def IsSimple (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ {n m : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)), ¬ HasTreeProperty T φ

/-- A theory `T` *satisfies stable forking* (Kim–Pillay; Peretz, Definition item 4) if for every
model `M` of `T`, every parameter set `A ⊆ M` and all tuples `a`, `b` of `M` with `a ⫝̸_A b`,
there is a stable formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` (i.e. `ψ(x, y, c)` with parameters `c` from `A`) such
that `ψ(a, b)` holds and `ψ(x, b)` forks over `A`. -/
def HasStableForking (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] [M ⊨ T] {n m : ℕ} (A : Set M) (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M),
    TypeForksOver L A a b →
      ∃ (k : ℕ) (ψ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) (c : Fin k → M),
        (∀ i, c i ∈ A) ∧ IsStableFormula ψ c ∧ ψ.Realize (Sum.elim a (Sum.elim b c)) ∧
          Forks A ψ (Sum.elim b c)

/-- The false formula `⊥` is stable. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isStableFormula_bot {n m k : ℕ} (c : Fin k → M) :
    IsStableFormula (⊥ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) c := by
  rintro ⟨N, _, f, a, b, h⟩
  simpa using (h 0 0).2 le_rfl

/-- The false formula `⊥` does not have the tree property with respect to any theory. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_hasTreeProperty_bot {n m : ℕ} (T : L.Theory) :
    ¬ HasTreeProperty T (⊥ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)) := by
  rintro ⟨k, N, _, _, a, hbranch, -⟩
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hbranch 0
  simpa using hx 0

/--
**The stable forking conjecture for simple theories** (Kim–Pillay 2001; Peretz, arXiv:math/0412356):
every complete simple first-order theory `T` satisfies stable forking. That is, whenever
`a ⫝̸_A b` (for tuples `a`, `b` and a parameter set `A` in a model of `T`), there is a stable
formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)` such that `ψ(a, b)` holds and `ψ(x, b)` forks over `A`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem stable_forking_conjecture_for_simple_theories (T : L.Theory) (hT : T.IsComplete)
    (hsimple : IsSimple T) : HasStableForking.{u, v, w} T := by
  sorry

end StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable forking conjecture for simple theories

The conjecture says that every instance of forking in a complete simple first-order theory is
witnessed by a stable formula.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [A. Peretz, *Geometry of forking in simple theories*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412356)

namespace StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

open FirstOrder
open FirstOrder.Language

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory)

/-- A formula belongs to a complete type, via the equivalent sentence with named constants. -/
def Holds {V : Type w} (p : T.CompleteType V) (φ : L.Formula V) : Prop :=
  Formula.equivSentence φ ∈ p

/-- Two maps into the variables of a complete type induce the same type. -/
def SameTypeIn {V W : Type w} (p : T.CompleteType W) (f g : V → W) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : L.Formula V, Holds T p (φ.relabel f) ↔ Holds T p (φ.relabel g)

/-- A complete type of a sequence indexed by `ℕ` is indiscernible over the variables `A`. -/
def IsIndiscernibleOver {Y A : Type w} (q : T.CompleteType ((ℕ × Y) ⊕ A)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin n → ℕ), StrictMono i → StrictMono j →
    SameTypeIn T q
      (Sum.map (fun z : Fin n × Y ↦ (i z.1, z.2)) id)
      (Sum.map (fun z : Fin n × Y ↦ (j z.1, z.2)) id)

/-- A complete type `r` extends `q` along the variable map `f`. -/
def ExtendsType {V W : Type w} (q : T.CompleteType V) (r : T.CompleteType W)
    (f : V → W) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : L.Formula V, Holds T q φ ↔ Holds T r (φ.relabel f)

/--
The formula `φ(x,y,A)` divides over `A` at the tuple represented by `p`: there is an
`A`-indiscernible sequence starting with the `y`-part of `p` for which the corresponding set of
instances of `φ` is inconsistent. In a simple theory, dividing and forking coincide.
-/
def DividesOver {X Y A : Type w} (p : T.CompleteType ((X ⊕ Y) ⊕ A))
    (φ : L.Formula ((X ⊕ Y) ⊕ A)) : Prop :=
  ∃ q : T.CompleteType ((ℕ × Y) ⊕ A),
    IsIndiscernibleOver T q ∧
    (∀ θ : L.Formula (Y ⊕ A),
      Holds T p (θ.relabel (Sum.map (fun y ↦ Sum.inr y) id)) ↔
      Holds T q (θ.relabel (Sum.map (fun y ↦ (0, y)) id))) ∧
    ¬ ∃ r : T.CompleteType (X ⊕ ((ℕ × Y) ⊕ A)),
      ExtendsType T q r Sum.inr ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ, Holds T r (φ.relabel (fun z ↦ match z with
        | Sum.inl (Sum.inl x) => Sum.inl x
        | Sum.inl (Sum.inr y) => Sum.inr (Sum.inl (i, y))
        | Sum.inr a => Sum.inr (Sum.inr a)))

/-- The tuple `x` represented by `p` is independent from its `y`-part over `A`. -/
def IndependentOver {X Y A : Type w} (p : T.CompleteType ((X ⊕ Y) ⊕ A)) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : L.Formula ((X ⊕ Y) ⊕ A), Holds T p φ → ¬ DividesOver T p φ

/--
A formula `φ(x,y,A)` is stable over the `A`-part of `p` if no complete type contains an order
pattern `φ(aᵢ,bⱼ,A) ↔ i ≤ j` while having the same type on `A` as `p`.
-/
def IsStableOver {X Y A : Type w} (p : T.CompleteType ((X ⊕ Y) ⊕ A))
    (φ : L.Formula ((X ⊕ Y) ⊕ A)) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ q : T.CompleteType (((ℕ × X) ⊕ (ℕ × Y)) ⊕ A),
    (∀ θ : L.Formula A,
      Holds T p (θ.relabel Sum.inr) ↔ Holds T q (θ.relabel Sum.inr)) ∧
    ∀ i j : ℕ, Holds T q (φ.relabel (fun z ↦ match z with
      | Sum.inl (Sum.inl x) => Sum.inl (Sum.inl (i, x))
      | Sum.inl (Sum.inr y) => Sum.inl (Sum.inr (j, y))
      | Sum.inr a => Sum.inr a)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- A formula has the tree property in `T`. -/
def HasTreeProperty {X Y : Type w} (φ : L.Formula (X ⊕ Y)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (_hk : 2 ≤ k) (q : T.CompleteType (List ℕ × Y)),
    (∀ branch : ℕ → ℕ,
      ∃ r : T.CompleteType (X ⊕ (List ℕ × Y)),
        ExtendsType T q r Sum.inr ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, Holds T r (φ.relabel (fun z ↦ match z with
          | Sum.inl x => Sum.inl x
          | Sum.inr y => Sum.inr (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n ↦ branch i), y)))) ∧
    ∀ (node : List ℕ) (children : Fin k → ℕ), Function.Injective children →
      ¬ ∃ r : T.CompleteType (X ⊕ (List ℕ × Y)),
        ExtendsType T q r Sum.inr ∧
        ∀ i : Fin k, Holds T r (φ.relabel (fun z ↦ match z with
          | Sum.inl x => Sum.inl x
          | Sum.inr y => Sum.inr (node ++ [children i], y)))

/-- A theory is simple if no formula has the tree property. -/
def IsSimple : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type w) (φ : L.Formula (X ⊕ Y)), ¬ HasTreeProperty T φ

/--
The stable forking conjecture for simple theories states the following precise version. Let `T` be
any complete simple first-order theory, and let `a`, `b`, and `A` be possibly imaginary tuples and
a parameter set. If `a` is not independent from `b` over `A`, then some stable formula

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The stable forking conjecture for simple theories

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory. $T$ is *simple* if no formula has the tree property.
A formula $\varphi(x, y)$ is *stable* if there are no sequences $(a_i)_{i < \omega}$,
$(b_j)_{j < \omega}$ (in a model of $T$) with $\varphi(a_i, b_j)$ if and only if $i \le j$.
An instance of forking $a \not\perp_A b$ is *stable* if it is witnessed by a stable formula, i.e.
there is a stable formula $\psi(x, y) \in L(A)$ such that $\psi(a, b)$ holds and $\psi(x, b)$
forks over $A$. The theory $T$ *satisfies stable forking* if every instance of forking is stable.

The **stable forking conjecture** (Kim–Pillay) asserts that every simple theory satisfies stable
forking. We follow the formulation of Peretz (Definition, items 3–4 and the following sentence).
The conjecture exists in several inequivalent published forms; this file states the one above.

Elements are finite tuples of a model. Since the statement is quantified over all complete simple
theories, the version for (possibly imaginary) elements follows by applying it to $T^{eq}$, which is
itself a complete simple theory. Consistency of an infinite set of formulas is finite
satisfiability, and witnesses that need not exist in a given model (indiscernible sequences,
order-property sequences, parameters of forking formulas) are taken in an elementary extension.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [A. Peretz, *Geometry of forking in simple theories*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412356)
- B. Kim, A. Pillay, *Around stable forking*, Fund. Math. 170 (2001), 107–118.
-/

namespace StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {M : Type w} [L.Structure M]

/-- The set of formulas `{φ(x, b i) : i : ι}` with parameters from `M` is *consistent*, i.e. it is
finitely satisfiable in `M` (equivalently, by compactness, it is realized in some elementary
extension of `M`). -/
def IsConsistent {n : ℕ} {β ι : Type} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (b : ι → β → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Finset ι, ∃ x : Fin n → M, ∀ i ∈ s, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (b i))

variable (L) in
/-- A sequence `s` of `β`-tuples from `M` is *indiscernible over* `B ⊆ M`: any two strictly
increasing finite subsequences of the same length satisfy the same `L`-formulas with parameters
from `B`. -/
def IsIndiscernibleOver {β : Type} (B : Set M) (s : ℕ → β → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k p : ℕ) (ψ : L.Formula ((Fin k × β) ⊕ Fin p)) (c : Fin p → M), (∀ i, c i ∈ B) →
    ∀ i j : Fin k → ℕ, StrictMono i → StrictMono j →
      (ψ.Realize (Sum.elim (fun q => s (i q.1) q.2) c) ↔
        ψ.Realize (Sum.elim (fun q => s (j q.1) q.2) c))

/-- A constant sequence is indiscernible over any set. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isIndiscernibleOver_const {β : Type} (B : Set M) (t : β → M) :
    IsIndiscernibleOver L B fun _ => t :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ => Iff.rfl

/-- The formula `φ(x, b)` *divides over* `A`: in some elementary extension `N` of `M` there is an
`A`-indiscernible sequence `(b_i)_{i < ω}` with `b_0 = b` such that `{φ(x, b_i) : i < ω}` is
inconsistent. -/
def Divides {n : ℕ} {β : Type} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (b : β → M) (A : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (s : ℕ → β → N),
    s 0 = f ∘ b ∧ IsIndiscernibleOver L (f '' A) s ∧ ¬ IsConsistent φ s

/-- The formula `φ(x, b)` *forks over* `A`: in some elementary extension `N` of `M`, `φ(x, b)`
implies a finite disjunction of formulas `ψ_j(x, c_j)`, with parameters `c_j` from `N`, each of
which divides over `A`. -/
def Forks {n : ℕ} {β : Type} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ β)) (b : β → M) (A : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N) (r : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ)
    (ψ : ∀ j, L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin (m j))) (c : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → N),
    (∀ j, Divides (ψ j) (c j) (f '' A)) ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n → N, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (f ∘ b)) → ∃ j, (ψ j).Realize (Sum.elim x (c j))

variable (L) in
/-- The tuple `a` is *independent from* `b` over `A` (written `a ⫝_A b`): no formula in the type
`tp(a / A b)` forks over `A`. Such a formula is an `L`-formula `φ(x, y, z)` with `z` instantiated
at a tuple `c` from `A`, satisfied by `(a, b, c)`. -/
def Indep {n m : ℕ} (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M) (A : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ (Fin m ⊕ Fin p))) (c : Fin p → M), (∀ i, c i ∈ A) →
    φ.Realize (Sum.elim a (Sum.elim b c)) → ¬ Forks φ (Sum.elim b c) A

/-- The formula `ψ(x, y) ∈ L(A)`, given as an `L`-formula `ψ(x, y, z)` with the parameters `z`
instantiated at the tuple `c`, is *stable*: there are no sequences `(a_i)_{i < ω}`, `(b_j)_{j < ω}`
in an elementary extension of `M` such that `ψ(a_i, b_j, c)` holds if and only if `i ≤ j`. -/
def IsStable {n m p : ℕ} (ψ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ (Fin m ⊕ Fin p))) (c : Fin p → M) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (N : Type (max u v w)) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : M ↪ₑ[L] N)
      (a : ℕ → Fin n → N) (b : ℕ → Fin m → N),
      ∀ i j, ψ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (Sum.elim (b j) (f ∘ c))) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- The formula `x = y` is stable. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isStable_equal (c : Fin 0 → M) :
    IsStable (Term.equal (L := L) (var (Sum.inl (0 : Fin 1)))
      (var (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (0 : Fin 1))))) c := by
  rintro ⟨N, _, f, a, b, h⟩
  simp only [Formula.realize_equal, Term.realize_var, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr] at h
  have h00 := (h 0 0).2 le_rfl
  have h01 := (h 0 1).2 zero_le_one
  have h11 := (h 1 1).2 le_rfl
  exact absurd ((h 1 0).1 (h11.trans (h01.symm.trans h00))) (by decide)

/-- The `L`-formula `φ(x, y)` has the *tree property* with respect to the theory `T`: in some model
`N` of `T` there are `k : ℕ` and a tree of parameters `(b_η)_{η ∈ ω^{<ω}}` such that for every
node `η` the set `{φ(x, b_{η ⌢ i}) : i < ω}` is `k`-inconsistent, and for every branch `σ ∈ ω^ω`
the set `{φ(x, b_{σ | l}) : l < ω}` is consistent. -/
def HasTreeProperty (T : L.Theory) {n m : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (k : ℕ) (b : List ℕ → Fin m → N),
    (∀ (η : List ℕ) (t : Finset ℕ), t.card = k →
      ¬ ∃ x : Fin n → N, ∀ i ∈ t, φ.Realize (Sum.elim x (b (η ++ [i])))) ∧
    ∀ σ : ℕ → ℕ, IsConsistent φ fun l => b (List.ofFn fun i : Fin l => σ i)

/-- A theory `T` is *simple* if no formula has the tree property. -/
def IsSimple (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n m : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)), ¬ HasTreeProperty T φ

/-- **The stable forking conjecture for simple theories** (Kim–Pillay, in the form of Peretz,
Definition, item 4). Every complete simple theory $T$ satisfies *stable forking*: for every model
$M$ of $T$, every parameter set $A \subseteq M$ and all tuples $a, b$ from $M$ with
$a \not\perp_A b$, there is a stable formula $\psi(x, y) \in L(A)$ such that $\psi(a, b)$ holds
and $\psi(x, b)$ forks over $A$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem stable_forking_conjecture_for_simple_theories {T : L.Theory} (hT : T.IsComplete)
    (hsimple : IsSimple T) [T.Model M] {n m : ℕ} (A : Set M) (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin m → M)
    (hab : ¬ Indep L a b A) :
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (ψ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ (Fin m ⊕ Fin p))) (c : Fin p → M),
      (∀ i, c i ∈ A) ∧ IsStable ψ c ∧ ψ.Realize (Sum.elim a (Sum.elim b c)) ∧
        Forks ψ (Sum.elim b c) A := by
  sorry

end StableForkingConjectureForSimpleTheories

Minor remark: the table labels the chosen form "Kim–Pillay/Peretz", but Kim–Pillay's original formulation is phrased via a type p ∈ S(B) forking over A ⊆ B, while the L(A)/fixed a, b form is Peretz's; I followed the explicit formulation given in the table's notes (Peretz, Definition item 4).
modeling_decisions: Version of the conjecture: the Peretz (arXiv:math/0412356, Definition item 4 and following sentence) form specified by the decomposition table — fixed a, b, A with a ⫝̸_A b, a stable ψ(x,y) ∈ L(A) with ψ(a,b) and ψ(x,b) forking over A — not the 'p ∈ S(B) forks over A ⊆ B with φ ∈ L' variant nor 'weak stable forking'. The docstring attributes the conjecture to Kim–Pillay and the precise form to Peretz.

Imaginaries: a, b are finite tuples of real elements of a model M and A ⊆ M is a set of real elements. Since the statement is universally quantified over all complete simple theories, the version for imaginary elements follows by applying the statement to (a single-sorted rendering of) T^eq, which is itself complete and simple; conversely the T^eq version implies the real version because forking, stability and independence of real tuples over real sets agree in T and T^eq. A reviewer should confirm they accept this reduction rather than an explicit formalization of T^eq (which Mathlib does not have).
Language is single-sorted (Mathlib's FirstOrder.Language); Peretz allows many-sorted languages, which reduce to single-sorted ones in the standard way.

Monster model avoided: the given model M is arbitrary, and objects that need not exist in M (A-indiscernible sequences, order-property sequences, parameters of the dividing formulas in the definition of forking) are taken in an elementary extension N of M, with N in universe `Type (max u v w)`; by compactness this is equivalent to their existence in a saturated model. Consistency of an infinite set of formulas is defined as finite satisfiability in the ambient structure.

Dividing: `Divides φ b A` = some elementary extension contains an A-indiscernible sequence (b_i) with b_0 = b such that {φ(x,b_i)} is inconsistent (some finite subset has no common realization); with indiscernibility this is equivalent to the k-inconsistent formulation.

Forking: φ(x,b) implies (in an elementary extension) a finite disjunction of formulas ψ_j(x,c_j), each dividing over A; the disjunction may be empty, so inconsistent formulas fork — matching the standard convention.
Independence: a ⫝_A b iff no formula of tp(a/Ab) (an L-formula φ(x,y,z) with y := b, z := c ∈ A, satisfied by a) forks over A; the hypothesis of the conjecture is its negation.

Stability of ψ(x,y) ∈ L(A) is taken with the parameters fixed at c and the partition (x; y): no sequences (a_i), (b_j) in an elementary extension with ψ(a_i,b_j,c) ⟺ i ≤ j (Peretz uses '≤'; the '<' convention gives an equivalent notion).

Simple = no L-formula φ(x,y) (any tuple lengths n, m) has the tree property, defined with a uniform k: in some model of T (universe max u v) a tree (b_η)_{η ∈ ω^{<ω}}, indexed by `List ℕ`, with siblings' formulas k-inconsistent and each branch (finitely) consistent.

T is assumed complete (`T.IsComplete`), as in Peretz's conventions. No separate nonemptiness hypothesis on M is imposed; an empty model (possible only for degenerate T) makes the statement vacuous since `¬ Indep` fails there.
Two short API/test lemmas (`isIndiscernibleOver_const`, `isStable_equal`) are included to exercise the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING's request for basic API tests.
